text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
RUDYARD KIPLING was born on this day in 1865. He was best known for his poems and stories about India, where he was born.
Queensland Magistrate HENRY CHESTER, who took possession of New Guinea for Britain by planting the UNION JACK at Port Moresby, was born in 1832.
British film director Sir CAROL REED was born on this day in 1906, best known for the films "The Third Man" and the Oscar-winning "Oliver".

American rhythm and blues singer BO DIDDLEY was born in 1928, and became a major influence on pop groups such as 'The Rolling Stones'. He was one of the early legends of rock'n'roll. His first hit was a double A-sided single "Bo Diddley/I'm A Man" in 1955. His greatest hit was "Say Man" in 1959.

US singer/songwriter DEL SHANNON (CHARLES WESTOVER) was born in 1939. His career began with his own program "Get Up And Go" on American Forces Network in Germany. Back in the USA he worked selling carpet during the day and sang in nightclubs at night. His hits included "Runaway" (1961), "Hats Off To Larry" (1961), "Hey Little Girl" (1961), "Swiss Maid" (1962), "Little Town Flirt" (1962) and "Keep Searchin'(We'll Follow The Sun)" (1964). He also composed hits for others such as "I Go To Pieces" for 'PETER and GORDON'. DEL SHANNON died on 8th February 1990.
Australian painter ALAN OLDFIELD was born on this day in 1943.

American guitarist, singer and songwriter MICHAEL NESMITH was born in 1943. He began his career as MICHAEL BLESSING and wrote songs for artists such as the 'Stone Poneys'. In 1965 he answered a newspaper advertisement looking for "four crazy characters". The end result was the manufactured 'Monkees'. Those rejected for the group included STEPHEN STILLS, DANNY HUTTON of 'Three Dog Night' fame, and convicted murderer CHARLES MANSON. After the 'Monkees' split MICHAEL went on to form 'MICHAEL NESMITH and The First National Band'. His hits included "Joanne" in 1970 and "Rio" in 1977. He did not participate in any 'Monkees' reunions.
Today is also the birthday of another 'Monkees' member, DAVY JONES, who was born in 1945.

British comedienne TRACY ULLMAN, who was also successful in America, was born in 1959. She began her career in London in the "ELVIS" stage show alongside SHAKIN STEVENS. In the early eighties she starred in the BBC TV series "Three Of A Kind". She then secured a recording contract and had hits with "Breakaway" (1983) and "They Don't Know" (1983) and "Move Over Darling" (1983). TRACY then moved to the USA and had a hit with her TV comedy "The TRACY ULLMAN Show".
** EVENTS **
1879 : The GILBERT and SULLIVAN musical "The Pirates Of Penzance" was performed for the first time in Britain.
1903 : A fire broke-out in a Chicago theatre, killing 578 people.
1916 : The indestructible mad monk GRIGORY RASPUTIN died on this day after his would-be murderers fed him cakes laced with cyanide, shot him, tied him up and threw him into an icy creek.
1922 : Soviet Russia was renamed the UNION OF SOVIET SOCIALIST REPUBLICS.

1945 : Two yachts "Rani" and "Horizon" went missing in the Sydney to Hobart yacht race. The two were found three days later in Bass Strait after the RAAF joined the search. "Rani" went on to win the race.
1946 : Australia's population stood at seven and a half million.

1962 : Scientists announced that Queensland's Great Barrier Reef was under threat from the crown of thorn starfish. The spiked creature feeds off the coral and an infestation had been located in an area stretching from Cairns south to Townsville. At this stage little was known about the starfish and how much damage had been done. It was believed that the only way to deal with the threat was to prise the individual starfish off the reef and remove them from the area.

1967 : HO CHI MINH, the North Vietnamese communist leader, sent a New Year greeting to anti-war protestors in the United States. More than one million US troops were engaged in the Vietnam War, which began in 1954 and ended in 1975. Americans entered the war in 1964 with the aim of stopping the spread of communism.
1975 : Australian fast bowlers JEFF THOMSON and DENNIS LILLEE took 13 wickets in Australia's third Test win.
1979 : RICHARD ROGERS, best known for his musical compositions with OSCAR HAMMERSTEIN the second such as "The King And I" and "The Sound Of Music", died today in New York at the age of 77.
1988 : Colonel OLIVER NORTH subpoenaed President RONALD REAGAN and Vice-President GEORGE BUSH to testify in the IRAN-CONTRA trial.
